work_title_english: Instruction in Measurement, with Compass and Straightedge, in Lines, Planes, and Whole Solid Bodies

author: Albrecht Dürer (1471–1528)
place_and_year: Nuremberg, 1525 (1st ed.); Nuremberg, 1538 (posthumous 2nd ed., Hieronymus Andreae / Formschneider)

witnesses.title: Underweysung der Messung (Editio Princeps, Nuremberg 1525)
witnesses.repository: Sächsische Landesbibliothek – Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek Dresden (SLUB)
witnesses.pages: 182 digital folio pages (sigs. A–Q, with Author's Errata on p. 182)
witnesses.role: Primary Early New High German copy-text and woodcut diagram authority

witnesses.title: Diplomatic Transcription of SLUB Dresden PPN 27778509X
witnesses.role: Collated diplomatic transcription preserving 1525 Nuremberg orthography (uᵒ, v/u, cz, ß) and figure numbering

witnesses.title: Underweysung der Messung (2nd Enlarged Posthumous Edition, Nuremberg 1538)
witnesses.notes: Incorporates expansions from Dürer's surviving working copy, including two additional Archimedean polyhedral nets and expanded perspective apparatuses in Book IV.

witnesses.title: Alberti Dureri Institutionum Geometricarum Libri Quatuor
witnesses.notes: Humanist Latin translation that transmitted Dürer's conic projections, polygon constructions, polyhedral nets, and perspective instruments across Europe to Cardano, Clavius, Commandino, Kepler, Galileo, and Monge.
witnesses.role: Latin terminological and mathematical collation witness

translation_provenance.english_track: Original GEOMETOR English translation prepared directly from the 1525 Nuremberg Early New High German editio princeps (SLUB PPN 27778509X), collated against Joachim Camerarius's 1532 Latin terminology.
translation_provenance.copyright_compliance: 100% independent public-domain translation; zero reliance on Walter L. Strauss's 1977 copyrighted English translation.
